topic.title: Development and Mechanistic Modeling of Visual Circuits
topic.overview: This topic asks how visual neurons acquire selectivity and how their connectivity supports perception. Computational models study cortical maps, ocular dominance, orientation tuning, and retinal processing using mechanisms such as plasticity, feedback, and cell-specific dynamics. These models link observable behavior to hypotheses about the organization of biological circuits.
topic.whyItMatters: A successful simulation can test whether a proposed mechanism is sufficient under particular conditions, but it does not by itself establish that the brain uses that mechanism. Combining anatomical or physiological measurements with task constraints offers a more demanding way to compare explanations.
topic.evolution: A 1987 mean-field account studies selectivity and ocular dominance in visual cortex. A 2001 model finds that simulated fixational eye movements can support the activity structure needed for orientation refinement. Recent representatives incorporate connectomes and differentiable biophysical models; a 2025 mouse-retina study combines cellular measurements with classification under varying contrast and luminance.
openQuestions: Which model predictions distinguish competing mechanisms of visual development?
How can task-trained circuit models remain faithful to measured cell physiology?
